description: Backend climate data integration and risk assessment engine - fetches climate projections from Open-Meteo Climate API, caches in Redis (graceful degradation to SQLite-only), calculates risk scores (flood/heatwave/storm) per meter location, generates mitigation recommendations, stores assessments in SQLite
steps: 1. Create separate SQLite database backend/data/climate-risk.sqlite with schema from design: climate_projections, risk_assessments, mitigation_plans tables with all indexes. Use better-sqlite3 with WAL mode. Register with databaseLifecycle.js.

2. Create backend/src/lib/climateData.ts: Initialize Redis client (ioredis) with lazyConnect and graceful degradation on error. Implement rateLimitedFetch(api, url, signal) with 1-second minimum interval per API using Map-based timestamp tracking. Implement fetchClimateProjection(location, scenario, hazardType, year) that checks Redis cache (24h TTL), falls back to SQLite (stale OK if <7 days), fetches from Open-Meteo Climate API (https://climate-api.open-meteo.com/v1/climate with lat/lon/start_date/end_date/models=CMIP6), normalizes response to ClimateProjection type, stores in SQLite and Redis. Export redis and redisAvailable flag.

3. In climateData.ts add getFromCache/setInCache helpers that gracefully handle Redis unavailability (return null/no-op on error, log warnings). Add SQLite fallback query functions getFallbackProjection(lat, lon, scenario, hazardType, year) that read from climate_projections table. Add Open-Elevation API integration (https://api.open-elevation.com/api/v1/lookup) for elevation data with same caching strategy.

4. Create backend/src/lib/climateRisk.ts: Export TypeScript types (ClimateScenario, HazardType, ClimateProjection, RiskAssessment, MitigationPlan, InsuranceTier, etc. from design). Import db from climateData.ts. Implement getMeterLocation(meterId) that queries deviceRegistry.listDevices({meterId}), parses location field (JSON {lat,lon} or CSV 'lat,lon'), validates lat ∈ [-90,90], lon ∈ [-180,180], returns {lat,lon} or null.

5. In climateRisk.ts implement calculateScenarioRisk(meterId, location, scenario) that fetches 2050 projections for flood/heatwave/storm, calculates exposure scores using formulas from design (flood: precipitation + elevation penalty, heatwave: temp anomaly / 5 * 100, storm: wind speed or precipitation fallback), computes overallRiskScore = flood*0.35 + heatwave*0.4 + storm*0.25, determines insurance tier, returns RiskAssessment object.

6. In climateRisk.ts implement assessMeterRisk(meterId, location) that calls calculateScenarioRisk for all 4 scenarios (RCP4.5, RCP8.5, SSP2, SSP5), returns worst-case (highest overallRiskScore), stores in risk_assessments table with timestamp. Implement generateMitigations(assessment) following design logic (flood>60→elevation+flood_barrier, heatwave>70→cooling+shading, storm>65→hardening+shutters), stores in mitigation_plans table.

7. In climateRisk.ts implement assessFleetRisk() that queries all meters via deviceRegistry, filters those with locations, calls assessMeterRisk for each, aggregates into FleetRiskSummary (totalMeters, riskDistribution by tier, averageRiskScore, highRiskMeters array, mitigationCoverage %). Implement getScenarioBreakdown(meterId) that returns all 4 scenario assessments from risk_assessments table.

8. In climateRisk.ts implement refreshClimateData(meterId, location) that bypasses cache and forces fresh API fetch for all scenarios. Implement getMitigationPlans(meterId) that queries mitigation_plans table. Implement updateMitigationStatus(mitigationId, status) that updates implementation_status and updated_at in mitigation_plans table.

9. Add unit tests in backend/tests/climateRisk.test.ts: test calculateInsuranceTier for all score ranges, generateMitigations for high/low scores, getMeterLocation parsing for JSON/CSV/invalid formats, coordinate validation edge cases. Add unit tests in backend/tests/climateData.test.ts: test cache TTL logic, rate limiting (queue behavior), API response parsing, error handling for 404/500/timeout.
acceptance_criteria: SQLite database created at backend/data/climate-risk.sqlite with all tables and indexes, registered with databaseLifecycle
climateData.ts fetches from Open-Meteo API with rate limiting (1 req/sec), caches in Redis (24h TTL), falls back to SQLite when Redis unavailable
climateRisk.ts parses meter locations from deviceRegistry (JSON and CSV formats), validates coordinates
Risk assessment calculates flood/heatwave/storm scores using design formulas, determines worst-case scenario across RCP/SSP scenarios
Mitigation recommendations generated based on risk thresholds from design
Fleet risk aggregation works across all registered meters with locations
All unit tests pass: npm run test in backend directory
verification: cd backend && npm run build - compiles without TypeScript errors
cd backend && npm run test - all unit tests pass
Check logger output shows climate database initialized
Manually test: node -e "import('./dist/lib/climateRisk.js').then(m => console.log(m.getMeterLocation('test')))" - returns null for non-existent meter
findings: Implementation complete. Created climateData.ts (Redis caching with graceful degradation, rate-limited API fetching from Open-Meteo Climate API and Open-Elevation API, SQLite persistence with WAL mode), climateRisk.ts (risk assessment engine with getMeterLocation parsing JSON/CSV formats, calculateInsuranceTier, assessMeterRisk worst-case scenario logic, generateMitigations with threshold-based recommendations, fleet risk aggregation, scenario breakdown), and unit tests for both modules. Database schema includes climate_projections, risk_assessments, and mitigation_plans tables with proper indexes. All functions follow existing patterns (winston logger, better-sqlite3, databaseLifecycle registration).
